descriptionChirho: The Hebrew proper name יִשְׂרָאֵל (Yisrael/Israel), the most frequent proper noun in the Hebrew Bible with over 2,500 occurrences. Originally the name given to the patriarch Jacob after wrestling with the divine being at Peniel (Gen 32:29), meaning 'God persists/contends' (from שָׂרָה + אֵל). Subsequently used to designate: (1) the patriarch himself, (2) the twelve-tribe confederation, (3) the united monarchy under Saul, David, and Solomon, (4) the northern kingdom after the schism, and (5) the covenant people as a theological entity. The multilingual evidence shows remarkable consistency: Israël in French, Yisrael in Spanish, إِسْرَائِيل in Arabic, इस्राएल in Hindi, and 이스라엘 in Korean. Prepositional forms (ב-ישראל, מ-ישראל, ל-ישראל), the conjunctive (ו-ישראל), and adversative constructions (על-ישראל 'against Israel') are all grammatical inflections of this single referent, not distinct senses.
